title: Sooty Mold on Tree Crops - Grenada

Header: Sooty Mold on Tree Crops - Grenada

Prevention: Monitor plants for the presence of ants and sucking insects and take action.
Prune plants with excessive branches to maintain adequate space and allow air and light movement through the field.
Keep plans healthy with nutrients but do not over fertilize.
Monitoring: Black surface growth on leaves, branches and fruit, that rubs of easily by the finger.
Whitefly, aphids, psyllids, leafhoppers, mealybugs, and soft bodied scale insects in shoot tips and back of leaves.
Distorted leaves that may indicate presence of these insects.
Sticky card board painted yellow or white can help trap some of these insects.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Place yellow sticky traps in fields as a means of monitoring and controlling whitefly, psyllids and leafhoppers.
Schedule annual pruning early in the rainy season.
Support the activities of biological control agents; such as parasitic wasps and lady bird beetles.
Direct Control (Chemical): When considering insecticidal control, always use personal protective equipment, and read and follow the pesticide label.
Do not apply to mature fruits or during periods of flowering.
